attempt: Tried: lowercase equivalence beyond COBOL words (literals, text words) is unstated.
reason: IV.4.2.2.1 p1 states equivalence for words; IV.4.1 p1 expands only nonnumeric literals, comment-entries and comment lines to the whole set; XII.2.4 GR5 and XII.3.4 GR6 carry it to text matching; VI.5.9.3 SR3 gives PICTURE's narrower equivalence. The unit's 'except nonnumeric literals' is the same line.
quoted: Each lowercase letter is considered to be equivalent to its corresponding uppercase letter

attempt: Tried: the character-set membership of colon is unstated.
reason: VI.1.3.1 p1 'colon (:) is permitted in level 2' and IV.4.2.1 SR7 make colon a COBOL character used as a separator; the format IV.4.3.8.4.2 writes it. Nothing further is imposed.
quoted: The punctuation character colon is a separator and is required when shown in the general formats

attempt: Tried: interchangeability including space is unstated.
reason: IV.2.1.6 p1 says comma and semicolon may be used anywhere space is used and are interchangeable; IV.4.2.1 SR2 adds the following-space condition. The unit adds no condition.
quoted: In the source program, these separators are interchangeable

attempt: Tried: an exception to the context rule.
reason: SR1b states the intersecting sets and context classification; the exceptions (LENGTH, RANDOM, SUM) restrict, and the unit claims no more.
quoted: The same COBOL word may be used as a function-name, as a system-name, and as a user-defined word

attempt: Tried: the SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS clause's own content is unstated.
reason: IV.4.2.2.2.3 item 7 and VI.4.5.4 GR8 define the figurative constant and its character; item 18 lists symbolic-character as a user-defined word. Nothing extra.
quoted: Represents one or more of the character specified as the value of this symbolic-character

attempt: Tried: a different bound.
reason: The unit says 160 and the rule says 160; the 120 is labelled history.
quoted: The implementor must allow for nonnumeric literals of 1 through 160 characters in length

attempt: Tried: a restriction on ZERO in expressions omitted by the rule.
reason: VI.6.2.1 p1 lists ZERO as an arithmetic expression operand; no narrower rule found.
quoted: the figurative constant ZERO (ZEROS, ZEROES)

attempt: Tried: uniqueness-if-referenced differs at level 1 versus 2.
reason: IV.4.3.8.1 SR3 gives uniqueness only for names explicitly referenced; VI.1.3.2 p1 covers the level 1 versus 2 difference. Same obligation.
quoted: uniqueness must then be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced

attempt: Tried: 'must provide the capability' versus 'permitted' differ.
reason: Level-2 permission of 50 qualifiers is the implementor capability; the level 1 exclusion is stated too.
quoted: 50 qualifiers are permitted in level 2

attempt: Tried: dimensions are not subscripts.
reason: IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR2 ties subscript count to OCCURS clauses (dimensions), so seven subscripts equals seven dimensions.
quoted: One through seven subscripts are permitted in level 2

attempt: Tried: relative subscripting semantics unstated.
reason: Format IV.4.3.8.2.2 gives the syntax; GR4 gives the increment and decrement meaning.
quoted: If integer-2 or integer-3 is specified, the value of the subscript is determined by incrementing

attempt: Tried: a rule forbids mixing.
reason: The subscripting format admits each form independently and no rule forbids mixing; SR2 constrains only order. Nothing extra imposed.
quoted: the subscripts are written in the order of successively less inclusive dimensions of the table

attempt: Tried: 'new method' imposes anything.
reason: The newness is history; GR4 and the format carry the leftmost position and length.
quoted: Reference modification creates a unique data item that is a subset of the data item

attempt: Tried: sequence-number content restricted.
reason: IV.7.2.1 p1 says any character; the digits-only is second-standard history.
quoted: may consist of any character in the computer's character set

attempt: Tried: a rule confines the following word to area B.
reason: p4 and p7 put the name after at least one space and do not confine it to area B, so beginning in area A is within the rule. Nothing additional.
quoted: the level-number begins in area A, followed by at least one space, and then followed with its associated record-name or item-name

attempt: Tried: separately compiled follow-on condition unstated.
reason: VI.2.4.4 GR1 and GR2 state the end and the separately compiled next program; VI.2.3.3 GR2 the termination requirement.
quoted: The end program header indicates the end of the specified COBOL source program

attempt: Tried: nesting needs more than permission.
reason: X.2.1 p1 states containment; the format X.2.3.1 carries the repeated source-program.
quoted: A COBOL source program may contain other COBOL source programs

attempt: Tried: 'same state as first called' unstated.
reason: GR3 plus X.2.4.2 items 1 and 3 define the initial state at first call and at each call of an initial program.
quoted: When an initial program is called, it and any programs contained within it are placed in their initial state

attempt: Tried: the call scope unstated.
reason: GR2 plus X.1.3.8.1 SR2 and II.6.4.1.2 SR3 state the scope.
quoted: A common program is contained within another program but may be called from programs other than that containing it

attempt: Tried: some listed optional part has no rule.
reason: VI.4.1 p1 covers the division; IV.6.2.3.1 brackets the Configuration Section and its three paragraphs; paragraph formats bracket entries; I-O-CONTROL format is bracketed too.
quoted: The Environment Division is optional in a COBOL source program

attempt: Tried: omission of condition-name unstated.
reason: The format brackets ON STATUS and OFF STATUS; GR2 says 'may'. Same permission.
quoted: the on status and/or off status of that switch may be associated with condition-names

attempt: Tried: IS may be required in SPECIAL-NAMES.
reason: Format VI.4.5.2 prints IS not underlined, so IV.2.1.2 p1 makes it optional.
quoted: Uppercase words which are not underlined are optional to the user and need not be written in the source program

attempt: Tried: STANDARD-2 as collating sequence unstated.
reason: GR4 is the ALPHABET clause's code set and/or collating sequence function and GR4a names the ISO 7-bit code for STANDARD-2; the summary adds no separate obligation.
quoted: a means for relating a name to a specified character code set and/or collating sequence

attempt: Tried: nonnumeric literal in a specific module unstated.
reason: SR3 of each I-O module says literal-1 must be a nonnumeric literal; XI GR1 gives the SORT association.
quoted: to a storage medium referenced by implementor-name-1 or literal-1

attempt: Tried: reach differs per organization.
reason: The same sentence appears in all three file-organization modules.
quoted: The OPTIONAL phrase applies only to files opened in the input, I-O, or extend mode

attempt: Tried: ORGANIZATION IS required in some format.
reason: The three formats bracket ORGANIZATION IS.
quoted: Uppercase words which are not underlined are optional to the user and need not be written in the source program

attempt: Tried: anything beyond the definition.
reason: The sentence is word for word in GR1.
quoted: The PADDING CHARACTER clause specifies the character which is to be used for block padding on sequential files

attempt: Tried: anything beyond the definition.
reason: Word for word in GR1.
quoted: The RECORD DELIMITER clause is used to indicate the method of determining the length of a variable length record

attempt: Tried: anything beyond optionality.
reason: Word for word.
quoted: The Data Division is optional in a COBOL source program

attempt: Tried: omission allowed in REL and INX unstated.
reason: VIII.3.2.4 GR2 and IX.3.2.4 GR2 make REL and INX clauses the same as Sequential; GR1c allows omission.
quoted: The number of records contained in a block is specified in the operating environment

attempt: Tried: a device restriction remains.
reason: VII.3.4 states no mass-storage restriction; only the USAGE DISPLAY and SIGN SEPARATE conditions.
quoted: If the CODE-SET clause is specified for a file, all data in that file must be described as USAGE IS DISPLAY

attempt: Tried: STANDARD assumption differs from GR3.
reason: GR2 defines STANDARD as labels conforming to implementor's specifications, so GR3 is the assumption.
quoted: If the LABEL RECORDS clause is not specified for a file, label records for that file must conform to the implementor's label specifications

attempt: Tried: anything beyond.
reason: Word for word.
quoted: Data-name-1, data-name-2, data-name-3, data-name-4 may be qualified

attempt: Tried: file connector case unstated.
reason: GR4 states the file connector case.
quoted: is external and may be accessed and processed by any program in the run unit

attempt: Tried: scope unstated.
reason: GR1 and GR2 define global name and the contained-program reach.
quoted: may reference that name without describing it again

attempt: Tried: FILLER in REDEFINES or group items unstated.
reason: VI.5.10.2 format shows FILLER with REDEFINES; VI.5.5.4 GR2 lets FILLER name any item; format VI.5.3.2 covers group items.
quoted: the data item being described is treated as though FILLER had been specified

attempt: Tried: zero allowed only when integer-1 is omitted or positive.
reason: Format 2 requires integer-1 TO integer-2 and SR5 allows integer-1 zero; GR2 range integer-1 through integer-2 then admits zero.
quoted: integer-1 must be greater than or equal to zero

attempt: Tried: level distinction.
reason: IV.7.2.2 p1 states it; VI.1.3.7 the level-2 allowance.
quoted: Any word, literal, or PICTURE character-string may be broken in such a way that part of it appears on a continuation line
